**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member onboarding** – no documented first-touch to first-class journey (intake forms, goal-setting, induction standards, coach assignment)
- **Churn/cancellation handling** – no win-back protocol when members pause or leave (triggers, outreach sequence, re-engagement offers)
- **Class quality audit** – no standardised way to measure coaching consistency, class energy, member satisfaction across instructors
- **Member check-ins** – no systematic cadence for retention conversations (30/60/90 days, quarterly goal reviews, at-risk flagging)
- **Referral programme** – no mechanics (who gets incentivised, what counts, payout terms, tracking method)
- **Data privacy & GDPR** – no documented handling of member records, consent, data requests, breach protocol (legal/compliance risk)
- **Supplies & sundries ordering** – no trigger points, approval limits, vendor management, stock thresholds
- **Incident/complaint handling** – no triage, documentation, resolution, follow-up standard (safety, disputes, safeguarding)
- **New quarter programme launch** – no playbook for rolling class schedules, coach prep, comms timeline, member migration

**Needs updating**

- **Coach onboarding/development** – likely missing gym-specific induction (equipment, client populations, safeguarding) and no clear progression ladder to Head Coach or Lead Coach
- **Member pause workflow** – if it exists, probably doesn't include pause reason capture (feedback goldmine) or re-engagement dates
- **Marketing SOPs** – 5 SOPs may lack integration with retention (no handoff from acquisition to member success team, no win-back campaign triggers)
- **Facilities** – 5/6 built; missing likely: emergency protocols, deep-clean schedules, equipment maintenance log + failure

# Service Menu Build — Execution Plan for Grace

• **Split this into two docs immediately, structured differently:** Coaches need a *fulfillment spec* (what they deliver, service standards, boundaries, upsells they can offer). Members need a *benefits matrix* (what tier unlocks what, price anchoring, comparison table vs. competitors). Don't force one template to work both ways—waste of time.

• **Price-anchor ruthlessly:** Before writing descriptions, research 3-5 Belfast/UK women's gyms. List their tier structure and costs. Then decide if you're premium/mid/value. Your menu copy changes dramatically based on this—a £45/month gym says "community access" differently than a £65 one. Lock pricing first.

• **Make the member doc *immediately actionable*—one-page visual:** Use a simple table (tiers × features) so a prospect can decide in 30 seconds. Include what happens *after* signup (first session process, app access, coaching booking). This converts better than prose descriptions.

• **Get coaches to draft their own fulfillment spec:** Ask each coach "what's YOUR service offer—1:1 coaching, form checks, nutrition advice, group classes?" in 15 mins. You'll find inconsistencies you didn't know existed. This forces alignment before the member-facing menu goes live.

• **Lock it in a shared doc, not email chaos:** Google Sheet or Notion, one source of truth. Links it into your booking system/website *today*—don't wait for "the rebrand." Outdated menus kill credibility faster than no menu.

You need to know: what's the lifetime value of a converted member? If it's £500+, you can afford to spend £50/lead and still win. If it's £150, you're already near ceiling.

3. **The conversion cliff is real.** You got 215 leads but only 29 sales (13.5% of leads). April–June had *zero* sales despite 127 leads total.
